title: Context Pooling: Query-specific Graph Pooling for Generic Inductive Link Prediction in Knowledge Graphs

problem.claim: Vanilla graph aggregation does not significantly affect the performance of GNN-based models for knowledge-graph link prediction.

gap.claim: Existing approaches lack graph-pooling methods for knowledge graphs and query-specific graphs for inductive link prediction with unseen test entities.

contributions.claim: Introduces Context Pooling to enhance GNN-based models for link prediction in knowledge graphs.
Uses neighborhood precision and neighborhood recall to identify logically relevant neighbors for each query.
Enables generation of query-specific graphs for inductive settings with unseen test entities.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The method was applied to two state-of-the-art models on three public transductive and inductive datasets.
The authors report state-of-the-art performance in 42 of 48 settings.

narrative_sequence.summary: Vanilla aggregation has limited reported impact on knowledge-graph link-prediction performance.
The paper introduces Context Pooling to improve GNN-based link prediction.
The authors characterize the method as the first graph-pooling methodology for knowledge graphs and the first to generate query-specific graphs for inductive settings.
Neighborhood precision and recall guide selection of logically relevant neighbors for each query.
The method is evaluated across models and datasets, with the authors reporting state-of-the-art results in 42 of 48 settings.

source_observation.claim: Query-specific neighborhood selection can be used to focus link-prediction models on logically relevant graph context.

interpretation.claim: Conditioning graph structure on the prediction query may improve the usefulness of message-passing context, especially when test entities are unseen.

application.claim: For inductive graph prediction, evaluate methods that construct or pool neighborhoods separately for each query.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the reported approach generalizes beyond the evaluated models, datasets, or knowledge-graph link-prediction task.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the two evaluated models or three datasets.
The abstract does not define the neighborhood precision and recall metrics.
The abstract does not provide per-setting results, baselines, or statistical validation details.
